name: Learn to surf
blurb: Standing up is the easy part. Surfing is mostly paddling fitness, wave reading and positioning — expect several sessions before a clean ride, and take a lesson so you learn the safety rules from someone who knows the break.
gear: A big soft-top board, 8 ft or more — small boards make learning far harder
A lesson at a beginner-friendly beach
steps: Learn the safety rules first: rip currents, how to fall flat rather than dive, never surface head-first, and never let the board come between you and a wave.
Learn the etiquette: the surfer closest to the peak has right of way, do not drop in, do not paddle through the takeoff zone.
Practise the pop-up on dry land until it is one movement — chest up, feet under you, no knees.
Start in white water on a big board, catching broken waves straight to the beach until standing is automatic.
Learn to paddle properly: lie centred so the nose is a few centimetres clear, and paddle deep and long.
Move to unbroken green waves only once you can pop up reliably, and learn to read where the wave will break.
tips: Being too far back on the board makes it impossible to catch anything; too far forward and you nosedive.
Paddling fitness is the real limit for beginners. Swim between sessions.
Learn to identify a rip before you enter the water, at every new beach.
proof: You paddle out, catch an unbroken wave, pop up and ride it along the face to the end.
